title: Artifact-driven LLM integration for mouseless design workflows
task: 自然语言驱动的专业建筑设计与数字工具生成
inputData: 自然语言设计指令 + 专业建筑设计任务上下文 + 对话式编程中的代码、错误反馈与BIM工作流信息
contribution: 通过真实专业设计竞赛的三个月mouseless design实验，提出artifact-driven方法，将LLM从直接几何生成器重新定位为定制数字设计工具（digital jigs）的生成器，并通过自学习与5S提示策略扩展复杂BIM工作流。
abstract: A three-month professional design experiment tested natural language as the primary computer interface while a team developed a 2,765.55 m² sports complex competition entry. Analysis of 2,162 conversation turns, 1,281 team messages and an 84-page design journal revealed severe weaknesses in direct geometric reasoning but showed that conversational programming and artifact-driven custom tool creation could support an end-to-end architectural workflow.
methodology: The study uses participatory action research over a 79-day professional design project. Natural-language LLM interactions were used across transitions from requirements to spatial configuration, floor plans, 3D object-oriented models and final deliverables. When direct design generation failed, the team used conversational programming to create reusable interactive digital artifacts or digital jigs for geometric and logic tasks, together with self-learning workflows and the 5S prompting framework. Evidence was triangulated from 13 prompt chains containing 2,162 user–LLM interactions, 1,281 project-team messages and an 84-page design journal.
results: The project was successfully completed and submitted, but 86.9% of individual LLM interactions were unsuccessful, with spatial reasoning and geometry handling as the dominant weaknesses. Artifact-driven and self-learning strategies enabled the team to overcome many direct-generation failures. Statistical analysis found a significant association across prompting-strategy combinations (χ²(90)=156, Cramer's V=0.120), with terminology alignment acting as a success multiplier when combined with other strategies.
taskEn: Natural-language-driven professional architectural design and custom digital-tool generation
inputDataEn: Natural-language design instructions plus professional project context and code/error/BIM workflow information used during conversational programming
operationEvidence: LLMs generate executable/custom digital design artifacts and scripts that are used to create, transform, and refine professional CAD/BIM design outputs during the competition workflow.
